functionList.serverSideTypescriptFunctionsRunBy: Server-side TypeScript functions run by the stack's Edge Runtime, at /functions/v1/<name>.
functionList.name: Name
functionList.thereIsAFunctionOfThat: There is a function of that name
functionList.itStartsFromASmallExample: It starts from a small example; edit it, then deploy. The name is part of its URL.

invoker.aFunctionNameOptionallyFollowedBy: A function name, optionally followed by a path
invoker.aJsonObjectSupermixerAddsThe: A JSON object. Supermixer adds the service role key itself.
invoker.runsAsTheServiceRoleAnd: Runs as the service role, and is recorded in the organization's audit log.
invoker.fromTheFunctionOrFromThe: From the function, or from the stack's gateway if it doesn't accept Supermixer's key.

versions.theFunctionAsSupermixerFoundIt: The function as Supermixer found it before changing it: deployed before versions were kept, or changed outside Supermixer.
versions.restoredItTakesEffectWhenThe: Restored {{name}}; it takes effect when the stack starts
versions.noVersionsKeptYetTheNext: No versions kept yet; the next deploy is the first.
versions.theLast10VersionsAreKept: The last 10 versions are kept, also after the function is deleted. The audit log records each deploy with these hashes, so you can check what ran.
versions.theFunctionSFilesAreReplaced: The function’s files are replaced with the version of {{value}}, and the stack’s functions service restarts. The current files are kept as a version first.
versions.notShownSinceTheyArenT: Not shown, since they aren’t text: {{join}}

functions.savedItTakesEffectWhenThe: Saved {{name}}; it takes effect when the stack starts
functions.supermixerConnectsToThisStackSo: Supermixer connects to this stack, so it can't see its functions folder
functions.ifItWasDeletedItsKept: If it was deleted, its kept versions are below; restoring one brings it back.
functions.deployedChangesTakeEffectWhenIt: Deployed changes take effect when it starts.
functions.aFunctionNeedsAnIndexTs: A function needs an index.ts (or index.js) at its top level
functions.keptAsTheyAreSinceThey: Kept as they are, since they can’t be edited here: {{join}}
functions.deployingReplacesTheFunctionSFiles: Deploying replaces the function’s files and restarts the stack’s functions service (a few seconds, for every function). Secrets are in Edge Functions › Secrets. Function code can read the project’s keys, so deploying needs the same access as revealing them.
functions.itsFolderIsRemovedAndIts: Its folder is removed and its URL stops answering. Its last versions are kept on this page, so it can be restored.
functions.itsFilesAreDeletedAndThe: Its files are deleted and the stack's functions service restarts. Its last versions are kept, so you can restore it from this page.
functions.serverSideTypescriptFunctionsRunBy: Server-side TypeScript functions run by the stack's Edge Runtime.
functions.itsFunctionsAreFoldersUnderThe: Its functions are folders under the stack's volumes/functions, served by its main function; deploy them where the stack runs. Here you can call any function by name. Stacks created with “Create a new stack” list, edit and deploy their functions here.

functionsSecrets.lettersDigitsAndNotStartingWith: Letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit
functionsSecrets.supabaseAndSbNamesAreReserved: SUPABASE_ and SB_ names are reserved
functionsSecrets.environmentVariablesEveryFunctionOfThis: Environment variables every function of this stack can read with Deno.env.get(). Values are never shown again; each is listed by its SHA-256 digest.
functionsSecrets.setSecretsWhereTheStackRuns: Set secrets where the stack runs. Stacks created with “Create a new stack” manage their secrets here.
functionsSecrets.supermixerConnectsToThisStackSo: Supermixer connects to this stack, so it can't change its functions' environment
functionsSecrets.youNeedAdditionalPermissionsToView: You need additional permissions to view function secrets
functionsSecrets.theyTakeEffectWhenTheStack: {{what}}; they take effect when the stack starts
functionsSecrets.pasteTheLinesOfAEnv: Paste the lines of a .env file into a name field to fill in several at once. Saving restarts the stack’s functions service.
functionsSecrets.name: Name
functionsSecrets.savedSecretsTakeEffectWhenIt: Saved secrets take effect when it starts.
functionsSecrets.functionsStopSeeingItOnceThe: Functions stop seeing it once the functions service restarts.
functionsSecrets.functionsGetSupabaseServiceRoleKey: Functions get SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_SECRET_KEYS and SUPABASE_DB_URL, and can bypass Row Level Security.
functionsSecrets.functionsGetNoneOfThemThey: Functions get none of them: they act as whoever calls them, with the caller’s token and the publishable or anon key.
functionsSecrets.functionsNowActAsTheirCaller: Functions now act as their caller
functionsSecrets.thisTakesEffectWhenTheStack: ; this takes effect when the stack starts
functionsSecrets.whetherDeployedCodeCanActWith: Whether deployed code can act with full access. Without it, a malicious or careless deploy can’t bypass Row Level Security or read the project’s secret keys.
functionsSecrets.ownersAndAdministratorsCanChangeIt: Owners and Administrators can change it.
functionsSecrets.turnOffTheFunctionsAdminAccess: Turn off the functions’ admin access?
functionsSecrets.functionsStopGettingSupabaseServiceRole: Functions stop getting SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SUPABASE_SECRET_KEYS and SUPABASE_DB_URL. Any function that uses Auth’s admin API, bypasses Row Level Security or connects to the database directly stops working until you turn it back on. Functions that act for the signed-in user keep working.
functionsSecrets.bypassesRowLevelSecurityLikeThe: Bypasses Row Level Security, like the service-role key functions already have. Can’t create roles or change Auth’s and Realtime’s tables.
functionsSecrets.theLoginInSupabaseDbUrl: The login in SUPABASE_DB_URL, which every function can read.
functionsSecrets.functionsDonTGetSupabaseDb: Functions don’t get SUPABASE_DB_URL while admin access is off.
functionsSecrets.anyFunctionDeployedToThisProject: Any function deployed to this project, by anyone allowed to deploy, could then create roles, change users’ passwords in auth.users and read Realtime’s settings. Choose it only if your functions need administrative access.
functionsSecrets.functionsNowReachAsPostgres: Functions now reach the database as postgres
functionsSecrets.functionsNowReachAsServiceRole: Functions now reach the database as the service role
functionsSecrets.administrativeAccessCanAlsoCreateRoles: Administrative access: can also create roles and change auth.users and Realtime’s tables. Every deployed function gets it.

api.startWithALetterUpTo: Start with a letter; up to 64 letters, digits, - and _
api.aRelativePathOfLettersDigits: A relative path of letters, digits, spaces and . _ - @ + = , with no leading dots
